consensus.executive_summary: Synthesis of 6 solar microgrid research papers demonstrates strong agreement that predictive demand scheduling and droop inverter control prevent brownouts during sudden solar irradiance dropoffs. However, a sharp technological conflict divides battery storage strategies: centralized lithium banks offer superior frequency stabilization (Adeyemi 2024), but suffer rapid thermal degradation in tropical ambient heat (>38C), where vanadium flow batteries and passive phase-change cooling envelopes provide dramatically higher cycling longevity (Nwosu 2024, Diop 2025).
agreed_findings: Inverter droop control stabilizes feeder voltage and frequency across remote off-grid nodes (Adeyemi 2024, Hassan 2024).
Predictive load dispatch reduces reliance on backup fossil generators by up to 31% (Kiplagat 2025, Mensah 2025).

top_contradictions.headline: Storage chemistry controversy: Adeyemi (2024) favors lithium for frequency control, while Nwosu (2024) shows flow batteries prevent tropical thermal decay.

recommended_next_steps: Field-test hybrid lithium-flow storage architectures to capture both fast frequency response and thermal longevity.
Integrate passive phase-change thermal barriers directly into rural battery casing standards.
Develop offline edge dispatch heuristics that do not require cellular GSM connectivity.
